I've been growing cotton on this land for 20 years. My hands know this soil. My husband and son take work in town sometimes, so I manage most of the fieldwork myself or with seasonal help from neighbors. Cotton is what I know. It's what this land is suited for and what I can sell at the gin in town.

I'll plant all 7 mu with cotton again this spring, same as every year. I'll buy the hybrid seed from the township supply store — the same type I've bought the last several years. It performs better than the older seeds my mother used.

I'll plough the field first, then turn the soil with the rotary machine before planting. I'll spread compound fertilizer into the base before I put seeds in. Later, when the plants start throwing buds, I'll top-dress with urea. That's the pattern I've always used.

For water — I have the well. I'll irrigate about five times: once before planting to settle the soil, then during the seedling stretch, then when buds appear, when the bolls are swelling, and once more if late summer turns dry. The rains here are unreliable, so I don't skip the well.

The bollworm and aphids are the real worry every summer. I'll spray eight times over the season — I start watching early and don't wait until I see damage everywhere. That's cost me before.

I expect around 250 jin of seed cotton per mu if the summer is decent. That's what I usually get.
